Modified assessment incorporating finance and macro literature:
The FOMC acknowledges a sharp, negative shock from COVID-19 but responds with an aggressive policy package: cutting the funds rate to the effective lower bound, initiating large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanding repos, easing the discount window, deploying dollar swap lines, and eliminating reserve requirements. Consistent with New Keynesian and credit-channel research, these steps aim to dampen the financial accelerator by lowering external finance premia and supporting the flow of credit when firm and bank balance sheets would otherwise amplify the downturn (Bernanke–Gertler; Kashyap–Lamont–Stein; Oliner–Rudebusch; Gertler–Gilchrist). The statement notes falling market-based inflation compensation but relatively anchored survey expectations, aligning with work on credibility and inflation-forecast targeting that emphasizes stabilizing expectations around a symmetric 2 percent objective to reduce welfare costs from inflation variability (Svensson; Rogoff; Friedman–Phelps critique of long-run trade-offs). At the zero lower bound/liquidity-trap risk highlighted in the literature, balance-sheet policies and forward guidance substitute for conventional rate tools and can mitigate, though not eliminate, near-term output losses. Net tone: still negative due to immediate activity deterioration and weak investment/exports, partially offset by decisive policy designed to stabilize funding markets and anchor expectations.
